chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from al-Kinanī, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu al-Subbah, buying flour (refined wheat) is humility (or modesty), buying whole wheat is dignity, and buying bread is poverty, and I seek refuge with God from poverty.'

key_terms.ذُلٌّ: Humility or modesty (contextually often contrasted with dignity)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between buying flour, wheat, and bread in Shia economic ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a hierarchy of economic self-sufficiency, where processing one's own grain (wheat) signifies dignity (*izz*), while buying ready-made bread represents dependency (*faqr*). This teaching reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical independence and avoiding the subtle loss of status associated with reliance on others for basic sustenance. The Imam’s concluding supplication underscores the spiritual danger of material dependence, linking economic autonomy to spiritual resilience.
